points.description: States that a data member can be accessed from any member function inside the class definition (equivalently: data members have class-wide scope / are available throughout the class).
points.partial_credit: Half marks if the answer says data members are accessible within the class but does not make clear that any member function can access them.

levels.says: Says data members are accessible in the class, but does not make clear that any member function can use them.

points.description: States that a local variable can only be accessed inside the member function that defines it (equivalently: local variables have function scope / exist only within that function).
points.partial_credit: Half marks if the answer says local variables are local to a function but does not make clear that access is limited to the defining member function.

levels.says: Says local variables are local to a function, but does not make clear that only the defining member function can access them.

rubric.notes: Full marks require both distinct scope facts: data members are accessible from any member function in the class, and local variables are accessible only inside the member function that defines them. Award half marks for a point when the scope idea is present but vague or incomplete. No marks for an answer that confuses the two or says there is no difference.
